quote.after:
For the absolutely continuous curve conclusion (c), assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) as required by the cited causal-curve calculus and fundamental theorem. The other clauses use the given smooth observer structure, pointwise adapted-chart existence and finite compactness arguments, without these additional curve-calculus premises. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), and put $n=N/\sqrt{-g(N,N)}$. Write $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. In a chart $(U,x)$ put $v^a=dx^a(v)$, $v_s=(v^1,v^2,v^3)$ and $|v|_{\mathrm e}=(\sum_{a=0}^3(v^a)^2)^{1/2}$.

**(a) Adapted orthonormal charts.** For every $p\in M$ there are a chart $(U,x)$, $x(p)=0$, a radius $r>0$ with $U=x^{-1}(B_r)$, and $K\ge1$, such that on all of $U$
$$n=\partial_{x^0},\qquad g_{00}\equiv-1,\qquad g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}.$$

**(b) Cone domination.** The chart and radius in (a) can be chosen so every nonzero future causal vector at any point of $U$ satisfies
$$|v_s|\le K v^0,\qquad |v^i|\le K v^0\quad(i=1,2,3),\qquad v^0\ge K^{-1}|v|_{\mathrm e}>0.$$

**(c) Curve form.** Every future causal curve $\gamma:I\to U$ of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] has strictly increasing time coordinate, and for all $s<t$ in $I$
$$x^0(\gamma(s))<x^0(\gamma(t)),\qquad |x_s(\gamma(t))-x_s(\gamma(s))|\le K\left(x^0(\gamma(t))-x^0(\gamma(s))\right).$$
Consequently every spatial component satisfies the same bound, and the curve image is the graph of a $K$-Lipschitz function into Euclidean $\mathbb R^3$ over the interval $x^0(\gamma(I))$.

**(d) Flat minorant cone.** The same chart can be chosen so the constant-coordinate metric $\eta_{16}=-(dx^0)^2+16\sum_i(dx^i)^2$ has every nonzero $\eta_{16}$-causal vector $g$-timelike throughout $U$. If $q,q'\in U$ and $\eta_{16}(x(q')-x(q),x(q')-x(q))<0$, then $q\ll q'$ if $x^0(q')>x^0(q)$, and $q'\ll q$ otherwise.

**(e) General temporal charts: exact compact uniformity.** For any chart $(U',z)$ define its temporal locus
$$P=\{q\in U':\nabla z^0(q)\text{ is past timelike}\}.$$
For every compact set $K_0\subset P$ there is $L\ge1$ such that all nonzero future causal vectors based in $K_0$, with coordinate components and Euclidean norm taken in $z$, satisfy
$$|v_s|\le L v^0,\qquad |v^i|\le L v^0,\qquad v^0\ge L^{-1}|v|_{\mathrm e}>0.$$
In particular these bounds hold throughout any relatively compact $U_0\Subset U'$ whose closure is contained in $P$, equivalently whose time gradient is past timelike on its entire closure. Timelikeness merely on $U_0$ gives local bounds at each point and uniform bounds on each compact subset of $U_0$; it does not alone give a uniform bound on all of $U_0$.

No additional choice is used to select the pointwise linear bases or compact cone constants. Countable and Dependent Choice are explicitly required only for the general absolutely continuous curve clause (c), through its actual calculus suppliers.

after.claim: (A finite cover by causally convex dominating charts.) For each $p\in K$ choose a chart $U_p$ around $p$ of the kind [L2] and, applying strong causality [L1] to the neighborhood $U_p$, an open set $V_p$ with $p\in V_p\subseteq U_p$ such that every future causal curve with two parameter values in $V_p$ has its subarc between them contained in $V_p$. The sets $V_p$ cover $K$, so by compactness there are finitely many points $p_1,\dots,p_m\in K$ with $K\subseteq V_{p_1}\cup\dots\cup V_{p_m}$. Write $V_j:=V_{p_j}$, $U_j:=U_{p_j}$, let $x_j$ be the chart of $U_j$, and set $$M_j:=\sup_{q\in U_j}x_j^0(q)-\inf_{q\in U_j}x_j^0(q)<\infty,\qquad C_j:=\max(1,K_j)\cdot\Bigl(\sup_{W_j}\sqrt{\textstyle\sum_{ab}h_{ab}^2}\Bigr)$$ where $W_j$ is a compact coordinate neighbourhood with $V_j\subseteq W_j\Subset U_j$, enlarged if necessary to at least one.

(The visit of a causal curve to one causally convex set is one interval.) Let $\gamma:[a,b]\to K$ be future causal and fix $j$. If $s<t$ with $\gamma(s),\gamma(t)\in V_j$, then $\gamma([s,t])\subseteq V_j$ by the defining property of $V_j$; hence the parameter set $\gamma^{-1}(V_j)$ is an interval in $[a,b]$: whenever it contains $s<t$ it contains $[s,t]$. In particular $\gamma^{-1}(V_j)$ has at most one connected component and is an interval $I_j$, possibly empty.

(Length over one visit.) Assume $I_j=[\alpha_j,\beta_j]\cap[a,b]\ne\emptyset$, and let $c_j$ be the constant of [L2] for the chart $U_j$, so that $\sqrt{h(\gamma',\gamma')}\le c_j\,(x_j^0\circ\gamma)'$ almost everywhere on $I_j$ (the curve lies in $U_j$ there). Then $$\ell_h(\gamma|_{I_j})=\int_{\alpha_j}^{\beta_j}\sqrt{h(\gamma',\gamma')}\le c_j\int_{\alpha_j}^{\beta_j}(x_j^0\circ\gamma)'=c_j\bigl(x_j^0(\gamma(\beta_j))-x_j^0(\gamma(\alpha_j))\bigr)\le c_jM_j,$$ where the last inequality uses that the increase of a coordinate along an interval contained in its chart is at most the coordinate range $M_j$, and that $x_j^0\circ\gamma$ is nondecreasing.

(Sum over the finite cover.) The sets $V_j$ cover $K$, so $[a,b]=\bigcup_{j=1}^m I_j$; by step 2.1 each $I_j$ is an interval, so by subadditivity of the integral over a finite cover by intervals, $$\ell_h(\gamma)=\ell_h\Bigl(\gamma|_{\bigcup_jI_j}\Bigr)\le\sum_{j=1}^m\ell_h(\gamma|_{I_j})\le\sum_{j=1}^m c_jM_j=:L(K)<\infty.$$ This proves the main assertion; the statement about arclength-parametrized curves follows from $\ell_h(\gamma)=b-a$.

(Imprisonment form.) If a sequence of future causal curves $\gamma_k:[a_k,b_k]\to M$ has all images contained in the fixed compact set $K$ and $\ell_h(\gamma_k)\to\infty$, then no subsequence can be parametrized by $h$-arclength on domains of bounded length; equivalently, there is no family of $h$-arclength-parametrized future causal curves with images in $K$ and domain lengths tending to infinity. This is the contrapositive of step 4.1.
(Conclusion.) Steps 1.1, 2.1, 3.1 and 4.1 prove the length bound and step 5.1 records its imprisonment form.
